text:
B: Hiya! Oh, hello, is it Kirsty?
A: Yeah. Hi. Erm, hello.
B: Hello, I'm Nicola. Lovely to meet you. Did you get on all right with that puzzle thing at the start?
A: Erm, sort of. I ran out of time on the last one, so I don't know.
B: Oh, same. I think I just guessed the last two, if I'm honest. Can I just say, when they showed us the photos, you had a drawing on the wall behind you, of a canal lock. Is that one of yours?
A: Erm, yeah. It is, yeah.
B: I thought so. It's really good. I used to be a picture framer, so I always clock what people have on their walls. Sort of professional hazard.
A: Oh, right. Where was that?
B: Lancaster, a little independent framing and art supplies shop. Nine years I was there, till my back packed in.
A: Oh, sorry. I go up to Lancaster sometimes on the train. Just for the day, the castle and that.
B: Oh, where are you, then?
A: Burnley.
B: Not far at all, then. So is that a real lock, the one in the drawing?
A: Yeah, it's the one down from me, on the Leeds and Liverpool. I walk past it most days. I did it from a photo first, but it looked flat, so I went back and sat on the wall and did it there, erm, with the geese hissing at me. The stone on the lock sides has all these marks where the ropes have worn it down, from the horses pulling the boats, and I really wanted to get them in, 'cause they're sort of the history of it, aren't they? People don't notice them. Sorry, I'm going on.
B: No, not at all, that's exactly the sort of thing I love. Rope marks. That's gorgeous.
A: I'm not, like, trained or anything. I started a BTEC at the college but I didn't finish it.
B: Well, if it helps, I left my Fine Art degree after second year. I was twenty and skint and a bit of a mess. I'm doing it again now with the Open University, art history mostly. Halfway through.
A: Oh, that's good. Is it hard, going back?
B: Erm, the essays are. My first one came back with so much red pen. But it's sort of been the making of me these last couple of years, you know? Do you do much drawing now?
A: Most days, a bit. Mill chimneys, me cat. I put some on Instagram, but it's not under my name or anything.
B: Oh, you should, you know. Honestly, I've seen work at craft fairs that's not a patch on that lock. I do lino prints myself, and I'm trying to get a stall at a few fairs this year. There was an exhibition at the Storey last month, local printmakers, and I came out thinking, I could do this.
A: I'd love to try lino. Is it expensive?
B: Not really. You can get a starter set for about fifteen quid. The paper's the killer. Have you got a cat in that photo as well? I saw an ear.
A: Yeah, that's Moss. She's old. She knocks everything off the windowsill, she did a jar of pencils this morning.
B: Oh no! They know exactly what they're doing, don't they?
A: She does, yeah. Erm, can I ask, is it alright, do you think, to put art on there without a name? Or is that a bit...
B: No, loads of people do. Nothing wrong with it. Though I'd want my name on that lock, personally. I'd—
A: Is that the timer? Oh, it's...
